But step 7 point 2 states a wrong and tool-dependent fact as universal — "They are not electrical, so the automatic connect-module machinery does not apply to them. Conversion between a real-valued net and a logic net is an explicit converter somebody wrote" — which directly contradicts the pack's own dv-connect-module-discipline-debug ("A real-valued net is discrete in time and needs its own converter family in both directions", line 319-322; "real-number nets are discrete-time and take their own converter family", line 180-182). wreal nets do participate in discipline resolution and do have inserted connect-module families; the claim is true only of SystemVerilog user-defined nettypes. remaining: Step 7 point 2 (line 251-253) is technically wrong and contradicts a sibling: "They are not electrical, so the automatic connect-module machinery does not apply to them. Conversion between a real-valued net and a logic net is an explicit converter somebody wrote." wreal nets participate in discipline resolution and have their own inserted connect-module family (wreal2logic / logic2wreal); "no connect rule matched" on a wreal-logic pair is a diagnostic FROM the automatic machinery. dv-connect-module-discipline-debug lines 180-182 and 319-322 say the opposite. The claim is true only for a SystemVerilog user-defined nettype. It also breaks step 7 point 1's heuristic, since a transistor-to-real-number swap changes which converter family is inserted rather than removing the converters.

Step 7 (line 242) Greps the report for "the connect-module insertion lines" with no declared marker string; the Connect rules slot gives a rule set and a file, not an insertion-line marker, and the ordering forbids deriving it from the second Grep. Standing rule 4.
